To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BMS-275183 is a Pgp and MRP2 substrate, and that Pgp is involved in the brain distribution of BMS275183, but not pantoprazole.
BMS-275183 is a substrate for MDR-1 and MRP-2 and the pharmacokinetic and brain distribution of BMS 275183 is altered in mice lacking Mdr1a/b.
BMS-275183 is a Pgp and to lesser extent an MRP2 substrate, and that the drug-drug interaction with benzimidazole PPI is not due to an effect of the PPI on Pgp.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel taxane analog, BMS- 275,183, which is a substrate of Pgp and MRP2.
the interaction of the novel taxane analog BBS-275,183, a potential drug candidate, with the efflux transporters MDR1, MRP2 and BCRP.
the interaction between BMS275183 and PPIs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BMS-275183 is a Pgp substrate, but that it is not a substrate for PPIs at the dose employed in this study.
Pgp, but not BCRP or MRP2, is involved in the disposition of BMS- 275,183 in vivo.
BMS-275183 is not a good substrate for BCRG, and is a good substrate for Pgp and MRP2 in the in vitro studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Pgp mediated efflux of BMS-276,183 is the most likely explanation for the interaction between PPI and BMS-275183.
BMS-275183 is a good substrate of MDR1 and to a lesser degree of MRP2, but not BCRP in vitro and in the mouse in vivo.
the interaction between BMS275183 and PPIs occurs at a level other than Pgp, Bcrp, or Mrp2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BMS-275183, an orally available taxane analogue, is a good substrate for Pgp and MRP2.
the drug-drug interaction observed in clinical trials is unlikely to be caused by inhibition of drug transporters by PPIs.
BMS-275-183 is a substrate for Pgp and MRP2 in both, in vitro and in in vivo models.
